title: Small CLs
summary: Google's engineering-practices guide: small self-contained changes are reviewed faster and better, carry fewer bugs, merge and roll back more easily, and almost any large change can be split.

assertions.quote: It’s easier for a reviewer to find five minutes several times to review small CLs than to set aside a 30 minute block
Since you’re making fewer changes, it’s easier for you and your reviewer to reason effectively about the impact of the CL
The CL is not so small that its implications are difficult to understand.

verdicts.note: One vendor dataset shows higher revert rates under ten lines, plausibly from config changes; the pattern has not been replicated.

assertions.quote: It’s usually best to do refactorings in a separate CL from feature changes or bug fixes.

verdicts.note: Tangled changes are shown to confuse both reviewers and defect analysis, though no study measures the review-quality gain directly.

assertions.quote: A CL that adds or changes logic should be accompanied by new or updated tests for the new behavior.

verdicts.note: Widely adopted policy, but no study compares co-committed tests against tests landed separately.

assertions.quote: Authors who practice writing small CLs can almost always find a way to decompose functionality into a series of small changes.

verdicts.note: Stacking and vertical slicing work for most feature work, but generated code, large migrations and some refactors resist splitting.
